newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates rise as tightness remains.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates rise as tightness remains.

text.p: Interbank rates were firmer across the board due to an apparent squeeze of funds at the short end of the market, dealers said.
They said Bank Negara's move to siphon off interbank money last week had tightened liquidity, as had the thinning of foreign funds from the market.
A lot of short-term funds held by foreign institutions has been taken out, a Malaysian bank dealer said.
Some dealers said banks were also short of funds after overlending at the long end of the market last week.
One-week money was at 7.30/40 percent from 7.10/20 on Monday, two-week at 7.30/50 from 7.20 and one-month at 7.20/25 against 7.18/20.
Three-month money rose to 7.25/30 percent from 7.20/25 and six-month to 7.25 from 7.23/26, dealers said.
They said the overnight rate is likely to rise in afternoon trading as other rates have all been pulled up.
The overnight interbank rate on Monday rose to 8.5 percent against 7.5 on Friday.
